A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Multilevel neural simulation-based inference. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B support a reliable comparison; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: V3 reports original inference experiments on four simulation problems, together with training-time measurements, sensitivity studies, and ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: V4 retains original experiments on all four simulation problems and reports revised Ornstein–Uhlenbeck results, alongside the retained appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The MLMC training objectives, simulator coupling through seed matching, and gradient rescaling/projection in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The OU network-size and dropout revisions concern experimental configurations, not new method components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the g-and-k distribution, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, toggle-switch model, and CAMELS cosmological inference. The unequal-parameter-dimension OU scenario is also retained; no dataset, domain, or inference task is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same NLE/NPE baselines, fidelity-specific baselines, and TL-NPE comparator. The revised TL-NPE patience values are experimental settings, not changes in comparator identity or membership.

E3.justification: The OU comparison is substantially redesigned. V3 evaluates TL-NPE patience values 1, 20, 100, and 1000; v4 uses 20 throughout. The reported validation fraction changes from 10% to 20%, conditioner width from 20 to 32 units, and dropout from 20% to 10%. Evaluation summaries also change from scores per trained network to pooled run/test-point results. These are reported protocol revisions, not evidence of same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: The OU patience sensitivity study is removed, parameter-recovery evidence in Figure 7 is revised, and the unequal-dimension failure analysis in B.3.1 loses its KLD diagnostic. These changes are confined to OU; the budget-allocation and gradient-adjustment ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 OU training runs. V3's boxplots summarize 20 network-level scores, using median NLPD and mean KLD across 500 datasets. V4 pools runs and test points, changing what the displayed spread represents. It also specifies IQR-factor-4 outlier filtering for the main display and supplies an unfiltered appendix display.

E6.justification: The principal OU comparison is replaced: v3 describes ML-NPE as comparable to or better than the best-patience TL-NPE, whereas v4 reports ML-NPE slightly better on both metrics at n1=10 and TL-NPE slightly better at n1=100. Figure 7's recovery results also change. Table 2 removes KLD results of 0.98 (0.08) for ML-NPE and 1.05 (0.14) for NPE, while retaining the NLPD numbers. The revised OU settings prevent interpreting these replacements as same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, variance bounds, sample-allocation result, and gradient extension are unchanged. Theorems 1–3 and their proofs in Appendix A are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract's central efficiency claim and the theoretical and multilevel contributions remain unchanged. V4 removes the introduction's claim about TL-NPE hyperparameter sensitivity and the conclusion's advertised advantage of requiring no additional fidelity hyperparameter tuning.

C2.justification: V4 removes the explanation attributing TL-NPE patience sensitivity to noisy validation with scarce high-fidelity data. The unequal-dimension discussion also drops the compensating KLD advantage, retaining the NLPD failure and optimisation-instability explanation. The broader seed-matching and training-overhead limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies that TL-NPE early stopping applies at both fidelity stages and selects parameters with the lowest validation loss. It updates the OU hyperparameters but removes the explicit KLD-estimation recipe using 2000 reference-posterior samples. Code access, hardware, and general optimisation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. Positioning relative to Krouglova et al. (2025) is softened by removing the hyperparameter-sensitivity criticism and reporting comparable OU performance overall. The contrast concerning theoretical guarantees is retained.

P1.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix B.3 are locally rewritten, with corresponding introduction, conclusion, and caption edits. Section ordering and most prose remain intact; other changes include hyphenation and the arXiv version/date header.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces patience-dependent plots with two-method comparisons and different axis ranges. Figure 7 is redrawn, new Figure 8 displays the unfiltered OU distributions, and Table 2 loses a metric row. Subsequent figures are renumbered and some text and figures move; the remaining displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves transparency by specifying TL-NPE checkpoint selection and showing full OU distributions, while qualifying its comparative advantage. However, it removes patience-sensitivity evidence, the failure-case KLD results, and the detailed KLD-estimation recipe. Pooling test points also replaces the earlier view of variability across training runs. These benefits and losses leave the overall quality direction uncertain from the supplied PDFs.
